{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-oh-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"ec21826b9e6d6067add63ba9855c60c045e4974f20bae5523e496bbcbed3d5c7","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-oh-class-d:lineage:55","source_registry_sha256":"33124b165dc74fabcff4bbcd8fd15db36bbe4a69a10e7def76a9d71752a5128b","source_liveness_sha256":null},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Be alert","heading":"Be alert — C","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A15
Arrange regular eye examinations because clear vision is important for driving safely. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A15
A driver whose license has a corrective-lens restriction after vision screening must use those lenses whenever driving. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A15
Do not use dark or tinted corrective lenses for night driving. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A16
Fatigue means physical or mental tiredness and can result from strain, repeated tasks, illness, medicines or inadequate sleep. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A16
Fatigue can impair vision and slow a driver's reactions. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A16
Aggressive driving involves an intentional act that puts people or property in danger. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A16
Examples of aggressive driving include speeding, tailgating, unsafe lane changes, improper signals and disobeying traffic lights or warning signs. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A16
A distraction diverts driving attention by taking the hands off the wheel, the eyes off the road or the mind away from driving. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A16
Distracted driving can cause crashes that seriously injure drivers, passengers, pedestrians or other road users. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A16
Avoid phone conversations, texting, arguments, emotional passenger conversations and eating while driving. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A16
Before driving, make sure children and pets are properly secured. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A16
The handbook's adult-device section generally prohibits using, holding or supporting a phone or other wireless communication device while driving, subject to its listed exceptions. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A16
An officer who observes a violation of the adult-device restriction may stop the driver. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A16
For drivers older than eighteen, the stated hands-free allowance requires no holding or supporting the device and no manual entry of letters, numbers or symbols. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A16
The stated adult-device allowance permits activation or deactivation with only one touch or swipe. [A16]
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A17
The adult-device exceptions allow reporting an emergency to police, a hospital, a health provider, a fire department or a similar emergency organization. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A17
The adult-device exceptions permit holding a phone to the ear during a call if starting or ending the call takes a single touch or swipe. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A17
A listed exception allows adults stopped at a traffic signal, or parked along a road or highway, to handle a device during an emergency or road closure. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A17
First responders may use electronic devices as part of their official work under a listed adult-device exception. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A17
The listed adult-device exceptions cover utility workers operating utility vehicles in certain emergencies or outage situations. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A17
A licensed operator's use of amateur radio is a listed adult-device exception. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A17
A first adult-device offense within two years carries two license points and a fine of up to one hundred fifty dollars; completing a distracted-driving course can help avoid both. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0017]
